# Column

Contents: [Use cases](#use-cases), [Chart IDs](#chart-ids), [Minimal spec](#minimal-spec), [Data](#data), [Options](#options), [Annotations](#annotations), [Dense value labels](#dense-value-labels), [Sizing](#sizing), [Fixtures](#fixtures).

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-reference.mjs from the boardplot describe, list and fixtures payloads. -->

Grouped, stacked, or 100%-stacked vertical bars; stacked columns can integrate an external PY tick and derived growth. Type `column`.

## Use cases

- Revenue by year or quarter
- Segment mix over time
- Monthly actuals against plan
- Rank change of a few players between periods (ribbons)

## Chart IDs

- `column.grouped`: fixture `forecast-ci-column`
- `column.stacked`: fixture `stacked-net-line-negatives`
- `column.stacked100`: fixture `stacked100-survey-total-column`

## Minimal spec

```json
{
  "type": "column",
  "data": {
    "categories": [{ "id": "north", "label": "North" }, { "id": "south", "label": "South" }],
    "series": [{ "id": "revenue", "label": "Revenue", "values": [120, 90] }]
  },
  "options": { "unit": "$k", "title": "North revenue exceeds South by $30k", "source": "Illustrative data" }
}
```

## Data

A `cell` is a number, null or a value object; see [Value cell](options.md#value-cell).

| Path | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| valueKind | string |  | Default valueKind for all series. One of `'fraction'`. |
| categories | array | yes | Ordered categories defining the displayed columns or positions and positional value alignment. |
| categories[].id | string | yes | Category identity used to match keyed values and annotation anchors. |
| categories[].label | string |  | Displayed category name; defaults to the category id and supports line breaks. A date id or `date` without a label prints a short date such as 'Sep'. Day ticks include the month ('2 Oct', or 'Fri 2 Oct' where room allows). A separate row carries the year under day, month and quarter ticks. |
| categories[].date | string |  | ISO 8601 category date, yyyy-mm-dd; strictly increasing dates permit date-axis promotion where supported. |
| categories[].total100 | number |  | Authored quantity represented by 100%; otherwise percentage variants derive their basis from the category values. |
| categories[].gapAfter | boolean \| number |  | Extra band-step fractions after this category; true defaults to 0.5. |
| categories[].breakAfter | boolean |  | Category axis break after this category: a gap of at least half a band step with the straight break glyph on the category baseline. Series connectors and net-line steps do not cross it. |
| categories[].footnote | integer |  | 1-based reference into options.footnotes. The number is drawn beside this category label as the reference mark, and the note it points at keeps that number; a reference to no note draws nothing and warns, and notes the engine derives print unnumbered. |
| categories[].partial | boolean |  | Period still running, such as the current week. Bars and segments on it are hatched and line markers on it are hollow; marks keep their positions. A drawn key names the running category once as "<label> to date". With no such key, the frame adds that note. |
| categories[].role | string |  | 'total' sets a summary column apart: gap and divider before it, bold head and values, no ribbons or connectors into it. On stacked100 with all its cells null and total100 (respondent base) on every other column, it prints the base-weighted share Σ total100 × share / Σ total100 (a percent cell is the share as authored, a count cell's share is count / total100), not the mean of the group shares. A series with a null in some group keeps an empty total cell and warns total-not-computed. One of `'data'`, `'total'`. |
| series | array | yes | Series supplying values for each category, with optional reference series for comparisons. |
| series[].kind | string |  | Accepted for combo-shaped data. Ignored here. A kind that differs from the chart type is refused. One of `'column'`, `'line'`, `'area'`. |
| series[].axis | string |  | Accepted for combo-shaped data. Ignored here. A kind that differs from the chart type is refused. One of `'primary'`, `'secondary'`. |
| series[].valueKind | string |  | Multiply numbers by 100 into pct cells; explicit pct cells stay in percent units. One of `'fraction'`. |
| series[].id | string | yes | Series identity used by keyed options, annotations and legend entries. |
| series[].label | string |  | Displayed series name; defaults to the series id. |
| series[].values | (cell \| { categoryId, value: cell })[] | yes | Values in category order, or keyed entries pairing a categoryId with its value. |
| series[].scenario | string |  | AC, PY, PL, FC (or ACT, BUD, FCST). Controls scenario labels and paint conventions. |
| series[].direction | string |  | Whether increases are favorable; defaults to higherIsBetter for directional comparisons. One of `'higherIsBetter'`, `'lowerIsBetter'`. |
| series[].role | string |  | Data series or comparison-only reference series; references are excluded from the main plotted data. One of `'data'`, `'reference'`. |
| series[].colorRole | string |  | Theme color role used for this series when no explicit fill takes precedence. One of good, bad, warn, neutral, neutralLight, highlight, total, others; series-N for step N of the theme ramp, 1-based (series-2 is color.series[1]); or status-<key> for a theme status colour. A hex colour goes in fill. |
| series[].fill | string |  | Explicit CSS fill color for this series; remains authored across theme changes. |
| series[].unit | string |  | Unit of this series' values, used to check shared-scale compatibility. Without a format example, a $k, $m, k or m unit prints its labels whole from 100 up, in place of options.unit. |
| series[].format | string |  | Format-by-example for this series' labels, for example 1,234 or 1.2%. Overrides options.format. |

## Options

| Path | Type | Values | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| labelDensity | string | `'full'`, `'smart'`, `'minimal'` |  | Value-label density. Default 'smart': every value stays eligible. A chart with more than 12 categories, or with most labels wider than the band, ranks the first, last, highest and lowest value (ties: the first) first. The other values then use only their natural seat beside the mark; with none free they are drawn nowhere and left out of the note. Those four may take one step, and the note names any that finds no seat. A smaller chart keeps every value on the bounded one-step rule and names any that finds no seat. 'full' treats all values alike and names every one that finds no seat. 'minimal' also applies the shared priority gate. Seats stay inside the plot band and one step from the natural seat. All values remain in reading records. When valueLabels is set, it wins: labelDensity is not read for the value labels. |
| legend | string \| object | `'top'`, `'bottom'`, `'none'`, `'auto'` (or another value of its type) |  | Key position. Multiple series get a key by default unless visible direct labels name them all. 'none' hides the key and warns if names are missing. Subtitle and footnote mentions do not replace the key. |
| valueAxis.break | false \| object | `false` (or another value of its type) |  | No break by default or with false. Set { from, to, style? } for a straight value-axis break; the omitted span collapses to a fixed 12px gap when valid. Automatic placement is supported only by waterfall and pvm. |
| axisTitles | object |  |  | Title over the value axis when valueAxis.show draws it, in the top row left of the plot. A theme with valueAxis.titles derives 'Measure, unit' from subtitle.measure and a unit the drawn subtitle does not print, when none is authored. |
| axisTitles.primary | string |  |  | 'Measure, unit' title over the value axis, e.g. 'Revenue, €m'. |
| valueLabels | string | `'none'`, `'last'`, `'ends'`, `'extremes'`, `'all'` |  | Which values print, with line's choices: 'none', 'last', 'ends' (first and last), 'extremes' (first, last, highest and lowest; a tie takes the first) or 'all', chosen per series over the categories in their drawn order. Unset (default): every value is eligible and labelDensity decides. When set, valueLabels wins over labelDensity: each chosen value takes the one-step rule of 'full', and one with no seat is named in the note. A value not chosen is unlabelled by choice: the note does not name it, and the value axis is drawn so it stays readable (all modes but 'all'; valueAxis.show false turns it off). Authored cell labels and flagged anomaly periods print in every mode. Grouped only: a stack has no single value per category, so stacked and stacked100 refuse every mode but 'all' with value-labels-variant. Example: 24 monthly columns with 'extremes' print the first, peak, low and last value. |
| variant | string | `'grouped'`, `'stacked'`, `'stacked100'` | `'grouped'` | Vertical arrangement: grouped by default, stacked in raw units, or stacked100 as category percentages. Plain stacked series use theme.overrides.color.stack, not color.series. Set options.palette or series fill for categorical colours. |
| grandTotalLabels | boolean |  |  | Show category stack-total labels in addition to segment labels; default on for the stacked variant and off for stacked100, where every bar would end on the same share. true keeps the absolute total on a 100% stack. |
| sharesOfOneWhole | boolean |  |  | true declares every stacked series a share of the same whole, such as channel shares of all orders: the stack then has a total, and percent series warn non-additive-stack only where a category adds to more than 100. Stacked and stacked100 only; refused on other variants. |
| referenceStyle | string | `'tick'`, `'line'`, `'marker'` | `'tick'` | Reference-series mark style; defaults to tick. |
| netLine | boolean \| object |  |  | Per-category ticks at a cumulative boundary of stacked columns, connected by default. |
| netLine.seriesId | string |  |  | Series whose cumulative boundary receives a tick; omitted uses the positive stack top, or the negative stack bottom when no value is positive. |
| netLine.connectors | boolean |  |  | Connect adjacent category ticks as a stepped line; defaults to true for columns. |
| averageMarker | boolean \| object |  |  | Computed dashed average rule with a solver-placed Ø label. |
| averageMarker.scope | string \| array | `'all'` (or another value of its type) |  | Series included in the computed average; defaults to 'all'. |
| connectors | boolean \| object |  |  | Connect matching series boundaries between adjacent stacked columns. |
| connectors.style | string | `'line'`, `'dashed'` |  | Connector stroke: solid 'line' (default) or 'dashed', matching the waterfall bridge's dash. |
| connectors.scope | string \| array | `'all'` (or another value of its type) |  | Series boundaries to connect; defaults to 'all'. |
| ribbons | boolean \| object |  |  | Ribbon chart: translucent bands (S-curves when ranked, straight in sheet order) join each series' segments in adjacent columns. Stacked variants only. Only for ordered columns (periods, waves, age bands); between nominal groups a band implies a false flow, so use connectors. Ranked ribbons narrow the columns; names default to seriesLabels right-edge; bands stop at a gap, break or total column. Over 6 ranked series warn ribbon-crowded. Not a sankey: nothing splits or merges. |
| ribbons.order | string | `'rank'`, `'sheet'` |  | 'rank' (stacked default) stacks each column by its own values, largest on top; a crossing is a rank swap. 'sheet' (stacked100 default) keeps the series order, as an answer scale needs. |
| ratioTier | object |  |  | Below-axis ratio tier computed from normalized chart series cells; authored ratio values are not accepted. |
| ratioTier.id | string |  |  | Stable id for the derived ratio tier. |
| ratioTier.label | string |  |  | Quiet caption explaining what the ratio badges measure. |
| ratioTier.numeratorSeriesId | string |  |  | Series used as the computed ratio numerator. |
| ratioTier.denominatorSeriesId | string |  |  | Series used as the computed ratio denominator. |
| ratioTier.at | array |  |  | Selected category ids that receive a computed ratio trace. |
| ratioTier.format | string |  |  | Format-by-example for computed percentage points, e.g. '1.2pp' or '88%'. |
| ratioTier.direction | string | `'higherIsBetter'`, `'lowerIsBetter'` |  | Whether an increase in the computed ratio is favourable; controls semantic treatment where supported. |
| seriesRamp | boolean |  |  | true paints the data series on the theme's ordered ramp instead of its categorical palette, for series whose order is the encoding (acquisition cohorts, oldest first): the first series takes the full mark ink, each later one a weaker rung, and every rung reaches 3:1 on the page in the light and the dark scheme. A series fill or colorRole keeps its own paint. Default false. |
| othersShade | string | `'quietest'`, `'apart'` |  | With seriesRamp and a Rest series (colorRole 'others'): how the ramp sits beside Rest. Default 'quietest'. 'quietest': Others is the quietest part, so every named step has more contrast against the background than Others and none matches it. 'apart': named steps only differ from Others, and some may be quieter. If Others is stronger than the first named step, the ramp falls back to 'apart' and the chart warns others-shade-unavailable. |
| signColor | boolean |  |  | Paint each column good/bad/neutral by sign(value) × series.direction (zero is neutral). Under series.direction 'lowerIsBetter' the encoding INVERTS — positives paint bad, negatives good — so the chart brings its own legend naming the polarity in words; suppressing it with legend 'none' is reported as legend-suppressed-encoding. Requires variant 'grouped' with exactly one data-role series; anything else is refused with sign-color-unsupported. Cells with an explicit fill, a highlight, or the topN 'Others' bucket keep their own paint and report sign-color-overridden. |
| anomaly | object |  |  | Flag exceptional periods against a visible, named corridor. 'mad' applies the modified z-score \|x − c\| / (1.4826 × MAD) > k, which does not let an outlier inflate its own threshold; 'threshold' applies authored bounds with no statistics at all. TWO DIFFERENT NUMBERS, never conflated: c is the CENTRE of the judgement, which is 0 under the default baseline 'zero' and the series' median under baseline 'median'; MAD is median\|x − median\| and is ALWAYS measured around the actual median, whichever baseline is in force. So under the default the corridor is centred on 0 while its width comes from the spread around the median, and both numbers are printed. Needs exactly one data-role series and an absolute variant. Fewer than 8 non-null values, or MAD = 0, flags nothing and says so (anomaly-sample-too-small / anomaly-mad-zero) — no mean ± sigma is ever substituted. Every render emits the anomaly-method info warning carrying method, baseline, k (dimensionless), centre, median, MAD, scale, n and the flag count. The decision runs on unrounded values; if two periods print the same label on opposite sides of the cut, anomaly-flag-label-tie says so. This is NOT an SPC control chart: no run rules, no subgroup limits, no seasonality adjustment. |
| anomaly.method (anomaly branch 1) | string | `'mad'` |  | Use median absolute deviation to derive the anomaly corridor. |
| anomaly.k (anomaly branch 1) | number |  | `3.5` | Flag threshold on the absolute modified z-score; default 3.5, the published threshold of the modified z-score method with the 1.4826 MAD scale. Do not pair it with a 3.0 rule of thumb from a different method. |
| anomaly.baseline (anomaly branch 1) | string | `'zero'`, `'median'` | `'zero'` | Centre of the judgement. 'zero' (default) reads the input as an already-computed deviation (surprise vs consensus, net cash movement, residual); 'median' centres on the series' own median. The SPREAD is measured around the actual median in both cases, so derived.anomaly reports `centre` and `median` as separate fields — under 'zero' they differ, and a levels series hands to this rule will flag almost everything (anomaly-most-flagged). |
| anomaly.label (anomaly branch 1) | string |  |  | Names the rule on the exhibit. It is prefixed to the derived sentence, never a replacement — the median, MAD, k and corridor always stay printed. |
| anomaly.method (anomaly branch 2) | string | `'threshold'` |  | Use authored low/high bounds to flag anomalies. |
| anomaly.low (anomaly branch 2) | number |  |  | Flag values strictly below this bound. |
| anomaly.high (anomaly branch 2) | number |  |  | Flag values strictly above this bound. |
| anomaly.label (anomaly branch 2) | string |  |  | Names the rule on the exhibit; the bounds stay printed. |
| seriesLabels | object |  |  | Name the stacked series once, at the right edge of the LAST column or the left edge of the FIRST, instead of in a legend: the layers of a cohort chart are read off their own bars. Stacked variants only; a grouped chart keeps its legend. |
| seriesLabels.at | string | `'right-edge'`, `'left-edge'` |  | Where the names sit, on the middle of each named layer: 'right-edge' beside the last column, 'left-edge' before the first, right-aligned. |
| seriesLabels.only | array |  |  | The series that carry a name; without it every stacked series gets one, and the solver hides the ones that do not fit. |
| seriesLabels.cagr | true \| object | `true` (or another value of its type) |  | Series CAGR: each name carries its series' compound annual growth rate over the span, 'Product B +10.1% p.a.', with a claim record per series. The years come from the categories' ISO dates or year-bearing labels; a series with a missing value, a start at or below zero or a negative end prints its name alone and warns; an end of zero reads -100%. |
| seriesLabels.cagr.from | string |  |  | First category of the span; default the first category. |
| seriesLabels.cagr.to | string |  |  | Last category of the span; default the last category. |
| seriesLabels.cagr.format | string |  |  | Percent format-by-example for the rates, such as +0.00% for two decimals; default one decimal. |
| shareLabels | object |  |  | Where and how stacked segment labels print their share of the column: '30 (26.3%)' in the last year only. Adds the share to labels.segment in the columns named by only and drops it from the others. Stacked and stacked100 variants; a grouped chart has no shares and warns. |
| shareLabels.only | array |  |  | Categories whose segment labels print value and share, such as the last year only; the other columns print the value alone. Default every column. |
| shareLabels.format | string |  |  | Percent format-by-example for the shares, such as 26.3% for one decimal; default whole percent, one decimal under 1%. |
| events | object |  |  | Event lane and key. Events are annotations of kind event with at or date, an optional end or to for a period, group, detail, priority and, on column, combo and line charts only, items (more changes on the same date). Gantt events take one label and refuse items. |
| events.placement | string | `'auto'`, `'key'` | `'auto'` | auto uses lane then key, key uses key only. 'auto' (default) sets events in the lane above the plot where they fit and numbers the rest into the key below it; 'key' draws every event as a numbered marker with its entry in the key. Under footnotes: false there is no key: those events are left off and listed in the footnotes-off lint. |
| events.rows | integer |  |  | Lane rows for event blocks. Default by canvas width: 1 under 1080px, 2 from 1080px. 0 draws numbered markers only. A row gives way while the plot band left under the lane would keep less than 40% of the canvas height. |
| events.groups | array |  |  | Kinds of events, authored once: label, tone and glyph. |
| events.groups[].id | string |  |  | Group id that events name in their group field. |
| events.groups[].label | string |  |  | Kind label printed in the block header and the key, such as Out of stock. |
| events.groups[].tone | string | `'neutral'`, `'bad'`, `'good'` | `'neutral'` | Colour of the glyph, the marker ring and the period bar; default neutral. An event tone overrides it. |
| events.groups[].glyph | string | `'dot'`, `'triangle'`, `'diamond'`, `'square'` |  | Shape that marks the kind without colour; default by group order: dot, triangle, diamond, square. |
| events.keyTitle | string |  |  | Heading printed over the event key. |
| window | object |  |  | Display window for ordered periods: keep the last n categories. Means, the average marker and anomaly rules keep every source period, the subtitle says how many periods show, and a mean's Ø label names the periods it covers, 'Ø 40.4 (Jan 25–Dec 26)'. |
| window.last | integer |  |  | Keep the last n categories of the ordered series. |
| viewDomain | object |  |  | Zoom the visible categories. Means, the average marker and anomaly rules keep every source period. A mean's Ø label names the periods it covers where the plot draws fewer, 'Ø 40.4 (Jan 25–Dec 26)'. Refused with a category sort or topN, which break the period order. |
| viewDomain.x | array |  |  | Inclusive category ids bounding the visible x axis. |

Plus the [shared options](options.md). This type does not accept `valueAxis.log`, `valueAxis.reverse`, `categoryAxis`, `secondaryAxis`, `rowLabels`.

## Annotations

An annotation anchor is a category or item id string, or an object with categoryId plus optional seriesId, segmentId and edge (start, end, total); pointId addresses a scatter point. Category anchors, including from/to, take category ids, not category labels.

| Kind | Purpose | Required | Anchors | Optional fields | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cagr | Draws a growth arrow between two anchored points and computes the compound annual growth rate from their values and ISO-date span. |  | from: AnchorRef (optional); to: AnchorRef (optional) | suffix: string, default 'p.a.'. Text after the rate. period: boolean. Print the period before the rate from the anchors' category labels, '2014–2019: +5.8% p.a.'. Default true when the chart carries two or more CAGRs, so nested brackets are told apart by their text, false otherwise. | Omitted endpoints span the first to the last category, or the first to the last total on a waterfall. Resolved endpoints need a positive date interval from ISO dates or year-bearing labels and a positive start value; an end of zero reads -100%, and a start at or below zero or a negative end omits the rate and warns cagr-undefined. On a continuous time axis the years are the exact span between the two readings. An anchor on one series of several (seriesId, or a line category, which reads the first drawn series) names that series in the label, "Product B +10.1% p.a.", and the arm runs from that series' segment or point. In text, ${value} prints the rate with its suffix, so "CAGR 2014–2019: ${value}" keeps the computed number. Drawn reference series accept anchors. |
| diff | Draws a level-difference arrow between two anchors and computes either percent change or their signed value difference. | from, to | from: AnchorRef; to: AnchorRef | mode: relative \| absolute \| reversed, default relative. relative prints the percent change from 'from' to 'to', reversed the change from 'to' to 'from', absolute the value difference. | Mode defaults to relative. Relative and reversed changes need a nonzero base; negative bases use its absolute magnitude and emit a warning. Absolute mode reports the raw value difference. A hidden label removes its arm. Drawn reference series accept anchors. |
| delta | Computes the signed difference between an anchored value and another anchor or literal, then places a collision-managed label at the first anchor. | at, vs | at: AnchorRef; vs: AnchorRef \| number |  | Drawn reference series accept anchors. |
| note | Places authored text at an anchored data element through collision avoidance, with an optional icon or status chip. | at, text | at: AnchorRef |  | Drawn reference series accept anchors. |
| callout | Places authored free text at an anchored data element, routing a leader when displaced and honoring the preferred side. | at, text | at: AnchorRef | preferSide: left \| right \| above \| below. Side the solver tries first; the label keeps a leader when it moves. headline: string. A bold first line over the text, which then prints in plain type; ${value} in it prints the anchored value from the data. Example: "headline": "${value}", "text": "Peak in handheld-loom demand" prints 153 in bold over the words. arrow: boolean, default false. A thin arrow from the text to the anchored point; the first line sits level with the point, right or left of it, where there is room. Not with icon or status. Example: "arrow": true. | Drawn reference series accept anchors. |
| valueLine | Draws a reference line at an authored value or an engine-computed mean, with optional tolerance shading and attainment fill between the line and resolved actuals. |  | from: categoryId (optional); to: categoryId (optional) | value: number \| 'mean', default mean. A number draws the line there; mean has the engine compute it. valueKind: 'fraction'. Multiply a numeric value and its tolerance by 100 before layout: 0.35 draws at 35%. Independent of data.valueKind. Omit it for values already in percent points; not valid with mean. label: string \| false. Name plus value; ${value} sets its position. A number already in the name is kept once. false hides it. side: left \| right, default right. Side of the plot the label sits on. tolerance: number \| { low, high }. A number shades that distance on both sides of the line; low and high shade an authored corridor. attainment: boolean \| { seriesId, direction }. Shades each category between its actual and the line. | No anchor is required. Value defaults to mean. Scoped means are line-only: seriesId and paired from/to compute a primary-axis mean and limit its stroke to those bands; other types refuse scope fields for a mean. Numeric values cannot use scope fields except as a category clip with tolerance or attainment. A secondary-axis line needs an acknowledged secondary scale and an explicit numeric value. Optional tolerance shades a value-axis band; optional attainment fills between the line and resolved actuals. |
| indicator100 | Maps 100 through the chart's value scale and draws a side tick with a 100% label. |  |  | side: left \| right, default left. Side of the plot the 100% mark sits on. | No anchor is required. The chart needs a value scale that can represent 100. |
| abs | Reads the anchored data value and places its formatted absolute value in a collision-managed label. | at | at: AnchorRef |  | Drawn reference series accept anchors. |
| event | Places a dated event in the lane above the plot as a block with a pole to the data, or, when it does not fit, as a numbered marker with an entry in the event key below the plot; periods draw a thin bar. | label | at: categoryId (optional) | date: ISO date yyyy-mm-dd, in place of at: the event sits at the last category whose date is on or before it, and the block header and the key print it as d MMM. Every category needs an ISO date; a date outside the categories warns event-out-of-range. end: ISO date, with date: the event is a period, drawn as a thin bar to the end of that day. to: Category id, with at: the event is a period to the end of that category. group: Id of a group in options.events.groups, which gives the kind label, tone and glyph. detail: string \| string[]. Authored lines under the title, at most three in the lane; nothing is cut, a longer block moves to the key. items: { label, detail? }[]. More changes on the same date, after this event's own label and detail. The lane and the key draw a compact +N after the title; the hover card, the SVG title and description, and the interaction records list every item in full. placement: auto \| key, default options.events.placement. key numbers this event into the key below the plot. tone: neutral \| bad \| good, default the group tone, else neutral. Column, combo and line paint the glyph, the marker ring and the period bar in it; gantt paints a bad rule. | Exactly one of at (a category id) and date (an ISO date) places the event; end or to makes it a period. The event lane above the plot sets a block of group and date, title and detail with a thin pole to the data; an event that does not fit, a second event on one category and every event under options.events.placement 'key' get a numbered marker and an entry in the key below the plot, numbered in time order; under footnotes: false they are left off and listed in the footnotes-off lint. The full date, title and detail of every event stay in the SVG title and description, the interaction records and the hover card, whether or not the lane or the key prints the detail. In compact mode the lane is one row of numbered markers and the key packs "n date title" into as few lines as the width allows; where the plot would still fall under 80px the key keeps "n title" and the info lint event-lane-compact says so. options.events.rows sets the lane rows (default by canvas width: 1 under 1080px, 2 from 1080px); a row gives way while the plot band left under the lane would keep less than 40% of the canvas height. |
| band | Draws an inclusive category span as a shaded band or bracket, or a value-axis plan corridor, tolerance band or attainment fill, with a collision-managed label. |  | from: categoryId (optional); to: categoryId (optional) |  | Era shade/bracket needs inclusive category IDs. Corridor and tolerance use finite low/high on the value scale, with optional from/to as a category clip. Attainment needs a plan value and shades each resolved actual; missing cells are skipped. Divider applies only to bracket bands. Scenario AC/PY/PL/FC paints a plan corridor (default PL). |

## Dense value labels

The default `labelDensity: 'smart'` keeps every value eligible. In a chart with more than 12 categories, or with most labels wider than the band, the first, last, highest and lowest values (ties: the first) take their seats first, and the note names any of them that finds none. A smaller chart keeps every value on the one-step rule and names any that finds no seat. Other values use only their natural seat beside the mark, and are dropped without a note entry when it is taken. Stacked columns apply this rule to totals. Authored, highlighted and pinned values keep their rank. Use `labelDensity: 'full'` to treat all values alike and name every value without a seat. Labels need a free seat within one step of the natural seat. A value that fits can use an inside-end seat. Reading records keep every value.

## Sizing

Floor 480 × 270 px; fit `fill`.
Below 480 px wide or 270 px high, down to the compact floor of 280 × 180 px, the chart draws in compact mode; `belowMinimum: 'refuse'` refuses there instead.

Below the floor a render is refused with `size-below-floor` and the pixels it needs. `measure` returns the natural and comfortable size for a given spec; see [Sizing in the manual](../manual.md#sizing).
